title: Introduction to Drawing
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Pre-Technical Studies; not yet checked by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher; safety lines marked SAFETY in the library to confirm first; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Printing letters and numbers (outcome c) and drawing the lines (outcome d) are marked on the learner's sheet with the rubric; the questions test the rules.

skills.key_step: The learner explains why drawing is used to communicate (shows shape, size and detail that words describe badly, understood across languages) and tells artistic drawing (expresses ideas and feelings, freehand) from technical drawing (exact, to rules and sizes, used to make things).

floor.question: Name a shape with three sides.

representations: an artistic and a technical drawing of the same object
contexts: a house plan for a new classroom
a poster for a school play

board.do: Pin up an artistic drawing of a stool and a technical drawing with sizes.

board.say: Which one could a carpenter build from, and why?

board.do: Wait for the learner to mention exact sizes.

misconceptions.repair: Show a tailor's pattern, a house plan and a car manual drawing; name who uses each.

listen_for: It is not, words are always better
misconceptions.repair: Ask one learner to describe a bracket in words only while another draws it; compare with a quick sketch.
Put an artistic drawing of a chair beside a technical drawing with sizes; ask which a carpenter could build from.

misconceptions.ask: Which drawing needs exact sizes and rules?
misconceptions.repair: Make a two-column chart: artistic (expresses feeling, free) and technical (exact sizes, rules, for making).

checks.question: Which drawing has exact sizes and rules?
Give one reason drawings are used to communicate.
checks.answer: They show shape and size clearly

skills.key_step: The learner names the types of lines and their uses: thick continuous (visible outlines), thin continuous (dimension, projection, hatching and leader lines), thin dashed (hidden detail), thin chain (centre lines), thick chain (cutting planes), and draws them; the drawn lines are marked with the rubric.

floor.question: Is the edge of the door vertical or horizontal?

representations: a drawing of a block with a hole showing every line
line cards to match to uses
contexts: a drawing of a wheel hub
a bracket with a hidden hole

board.do: Draw a block with a hole: outline thick, hidden edges dashed, centre chain.
Point at the chain line through the hole.
Wait for the learner to say the centre.

misconceptions.repair: Draw both large: short dashes (hidden detail) and long-short-long (centre line). Say "dashes hide, chains centre".

misconceptions.ask: Which line marks the centre of a hole?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a hole: its hidden edges in dashes and its centre in chain lines, on the same drawing.

misconceptions.ask: Which line is used for dimension lines?
misconceptions.repair: Show that thick lines are only for the object's outline; everything added (dimension, projection, hatching) is thin.

misconceptions.ask: Which line draws the outline of an object?
misconceptions.repair: Draw light construction lines first, then go over the visible outline in thick lines.

checks.question: Which line is used for the outline of an object?

skills.key_step: The learner reads common symbols and abbreviations on drawings: Ø (diameter), R (radius), ⊥ (perpendicular), // (parallel), CL (centre line), A/F (across flats), A/C (across corners), I/D and O/D (inside and outside diameter), DIA, RAD, SQ, HEX, and illustrates them; the drawn symbols are marked with the rubric.

floor.question: The radius is 10 mm. What is the diameter?

representations: a drawing of a nut showing A/F and A/C
a pipe end showing I/D and O/D

board.do: Draw a hexagon nut with A/F and A/C marked.

board.say: What does A/F measure on this nut?

board.do: Wait for the learner to say flat to flat.
Write A/F and A/C with their meanings.

misconceptions.ask: What does R mean on a drawing?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a circle and label R from the centre to the edge and Ø across; write R 20 and Ø 40 for the same circle.
Draw ⊥ beside a T-shape and // beside railway lines; the symbol looks like what it means.
Draw a pipe end: I/D the hole, O/D the outside; "I for inside, O for outside".

misconceptions.ask: What does A/F mean on a nut?
misconceptions.repair: Draw a nut: A/F from flat side to flat side (the spanner size), A/C from corner to corner (larger).

checks.question: What does R mean on a drawing?

skills.key_step: The learner states and applies the printing rules for drawings: plain capitals, single strokes, all upright (or all at one slope), the same height between faint guide lines, even letter gaps and wider word gaps; the printed sheet is marked with the rubric.

floor.prerequisite: Knows that a technical drawing must be exact and clear.
floor.question: Who must be able to read a technical drawing?

representations: a good and a poor printed title side by side
a capital alphabet in single strokes
steps: Print each letter in capitals with single strokes.
Keep letter gaps even and word gaps wider.
Check every letter touches both guide lines.
contexts: the title block of a drawing
a label on a sketch of a stool
a sign-writer painting a shop name

board.do: Print "Front Elevation" on the board in mixed case, without guide lines.

board.say: Which two rules does this title break?

board.do: Wait for the learner to name capitals and guide lines.
Reprint it in capitals between two guide lines.

misconceptions.ask: How are notes written on a technical drawing?
misconceptions.repair: Show the same note in joined writing and in printed capitals to someone across the room; ask which they can read. Practise single-stroke capitals.

misconceptions.ask: Which title is correctly printed on a drawing?
misconceptions.repair: Write three titles on the board in mixed case and ask the learner to reprint them all in capitals between guide lines.

misconceptions.ask: What keeps all the letters of a note the same height?
misconceptions.repair: Draw two faint guide lines 5 mm apart with a sharp pencil; print between them; compare with a line printed without guides.

listen_for: The same, so the note fits in a short space
misconceptions.ask: How should the gaps between words compare with the gaps between letters?
misconceptions.repair: Print "STEEL PLATE" with no word gap and ask a partner to read it at a glance; then reprint with a clear word gap.

checks.question: In what kind of letters are notes printed on a drawing?
What are guide lines for?
checks.answer: To keep the letters the same height
